<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Cap LoRA shrink's configured split-K at the number of K blocks to avoid launching empty reduction programs. Fixes #61030; the proposed cap and original H100 evidence are credited to @ToukoUrsin. The final diff changes one production line; the added boundary test and its dedicated imports have been removed following review.

## Claims

- With the default small-batch config and K=4096, reduce split-K from 64 to 16, removing 48 empty programs per M/N tile and adapter.
- Preserve useful K-block assignments and the fixed batch-invariant partition. Configs already at or below the cap retain their split count.
- Local kernel measurements show lower shrink latency in capped cases. The small-model E2E measurements below do not establish a reliable end-to-end speedup.

## Validation

Local hardware: NVIDIA RTX 3050 Laptop GPU (4GB), Ubuntu 24.04 / WSL2, driver 592.82, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1. The removed boundary test is retained only as an external validation script and is not part of the PR or CI.

```bash
# Save the external validation scripts below outside the source checkout.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest /path/to/test_review_boundaries.py -v
# 16 passed in 15.81s: FP16/BF16; K=255/256/257/4096/14337/16384/32768, M=32/128.
.venv/bin/python /path/to/verify_baseline.py
# 10 expected launch-grid failures, 6 passed in 5.61s on the uncapped baseline.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_lora_shrink_batch_invariant.py -v
# 6 passed in 2.99s, including bitwise equality across batch sizes.
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py
# All applicable hooks passed; normal commit hooks also passed.
git diff 3e8e136...HEAD --check
# Passed.
```

Both boundary arms execute the real Triton kernel and compare output with the existing matmul reference. The uncapped failures are expected reproducer results, not failing candidate tests. The existing batch-invariant suite remains unchanged. Full upstream GPU CI, H100, AMD, and XPU validation have not been run locally.

Kernel A/B: FP16, rank16, scaling0.5, default config, includes output zeroing; same tensors and mapping, including a no-LoRA token. Each CUDA graph contains 200 shrink calls. Seven alternating A/B and B/A rounds each replay the graph 20 times; values below are per-call median microseconds, with min/max across the seven rounds. Both paths also pass an FP64 matmul reference comparison at rtol/atol=1e-2.

| M / K / LoRA slots / slices | Baseline μs [min, max] | Capped μs [min, max] | Median ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 32 / 4096 / 1 / 1 | 7.63 [6.14, 8.24] | 5.46 [4.66, 7.31] | 1.40× |
| 32 / 4096 / 16 / 1 | 32.69 [31.25, 33.30] | 21.23 [20.45, 22.66] | 1.54× |
| 32 / 4096 / 32 / 1 | 60.32 [59.44, 64.53] | 36.57 [35.80, 41.00] | 1.65× |
| 32 / 4096 / 16 / 3 | 189.02 [187.36, 196.05] | 70.96 [69.92, 75.19] | 2.66× |
| 32 / 256 / 4 / 1 | 8.91 [8.21, 9.08] | 3.75 [3.45, 4.66] | 2.38× |
| 128 / 4096 / 16 / 1 (uncapped control) | 23.69 [23.25, 25.15] | 23.87 [23.65, 25.50] | 0.99× |

The kernel measurements were collected on the preceding base `bd5bbce`; both affected source files were identical after rebasing to `3e8e136`. This microbenchmark calls independently compiled baseline and candidate functions and is unaffected by the E2E correction below. The original issue's H100 measurements are separate author-provided evidence.

**Correction to previously reported E2E evidence:** the old harness replaced the outer `inference_mode` wrapper's code object without changing the function captured by its closure. Both arms therefore used the capped implementation. The previously reported 1.3382s/1.3408s comparison and 0.01084149 logprob difference are withdrawn as baseline/candidate evidence. The replacement harness changes the underlying `__wrapped__` function and verifies the actual kernel partition arguments before timing.

Corrected E2E: pinned Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, synthetic nonzero rank16/alpha16 LoRA on q/v/o/gate/up/down, FP16, eager TRITON_ATTN, no prefix caching, four requests × 16 greedy output tokens, max_model_len128, KV cache32MiB. One configuration uses the same adapter for all requests; the other uses four distinct adapters, one per request. Adapter tensor hashes match across every arm.

Each configuration runs three alternating AB/BA rounds, with a fresh process and engine for each arm: 12 processes total. Each engine performs one instrumented warmup followed by three complete generations without launch recording. Times exclude initialization and warmup; they include prefill, decoding, sampling, and host generation overhead, with CUDA synchronization around generation. The table reports the median of three process medians and the min/max of those process medians. The GPU is a laptop desktop device; clock and background-load variation were not controlled.

| Active LoRAs | Baseline seconds [range] | Capped seconds [range] | Baseline / capped | Output tokens/s baseline / capped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1.1106 [1.0901, 1.1679] | 1.2851 [1.1079, 1.2924] | 0.864× | 57.63 / 49.80 |
| 4 | 1.2531 [1.0609, 1.4145] | 1.1358 [1.1243, 1.1537] | 1.103× | 51.07 / 56.35 |

All generated token IDs matched across the 18 measured generations per configuration (1,152 output tokens/configuration, 2,304 total). Across the first measured generation of each paired baseline/candidate round, the maximum generated-token logprob difference was 0.00814527 for one active LoRA and 0.01142752 for four. This is observed equality on four synthetic-adapter prompts, not a general accuracy or bitwise-determinism guarantee.

Warmup recording verified one/four actual active LoRA slots and baseline SPLIT_K=64 versus capped SPLIT_K=4/8/12 at K=1024/2048/3072, BLOCK_K=256, during prefill and decode. Recording and GPU-to-CPU metadata reads were removed before timing. The one-adapter capped median is slower and the four-adapter capped median is faster, with overlapping run ranges; these mixed results do not support a reliable E2E speedup claim. This is an in-process integration smoke test, not an HTTP concurrency benchmark or trained-adapter task evaluation; larger deployment workloads remain unmeasured.

## Details

The default config for M<128 requests 64 splits with BLOCK_K=256. When the configured split count exceeds ceil(K/BLOCK_K), only the first ceil(K/BLOCK_K) splits have valid K data, each with one K iteration. The cap removes empty splits without changing useful tile assignments. `EVEN_K` is recomputed afterward, and the existing batch-invariant override still sets BLOCK_K=256 and SPLIT_K=8.

Ordinary multi-split accumulation still uses floating-point atomics and is not bitwise deterministic. Reducing to one split switches to direct stores, verified locally at K=255/256. The change adds no device synchronization and changes no operator schemas or default configuration tables.

Duplicate-work checks repeated before this review update found only this PR referencing #61030 and no other PR implementing this cap. #59572 optimizes the M-dimension grid; #50278 forces split-K=1 for determinism; #58533 changes PDL shrink/expand overlap and explicitly excludes the separate split-K optimization. This PR preserves split-K parallelism up to the useful K-block count.

**AI assistance:** OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and this description. The human submitter previously confirmed reviewing the original changed lines, understanding the validation limits, and personally running the relevant tests. This review update removes the contributed test and corrects/supplements the validation evidence; no new human execution of these supplementary measurements is claimed. All three commits include `Assisted-by` attribution and `Signed-off-by` trailers.

"""Local-only GPU validation retained after upstream requested test removal."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd()))
import pytest
import torch
import vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops.lora_shrink_op as shrink_op
import vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops.utils as lora_utils
from tests.lora.test_punica_ops import (
    DTYPES, DEVICES, check_lora_shrink_kernel, set_random_seed,
)

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def restore_default_device():
    previous = torch.get_default_device()
    yield
    torch.set_default_device(previous)

@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", DTYPES)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", DEVICES)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "batches,hidden_size,nslices,expected_grid_m",
    [
        (32, 255, 1, 1),  # One masked K block; direct store.
        (32, 256, 3, 1),  # One full K block; direct store.
        (32, 257, 3, 2),  # Two splits with a masked tail.
        (32, 4096, 1, 16),
        (32, 14337, 1, 57),  # Non-power-of-two split count.
        (32, 16384, 1, 64),  # All configured splits contribute.
        (32, 32768, 1, 64),  # Multiple K iterations per split.
        (128, 4096, 1, 32),  # Larger-batch config: four M blocks, eight splits.
    ],
)
def test_lora_shrink_split_k_boundaries(
    monkeypatch, batches, hidden_size, nslices, expected_grid_m, dtype, device
):
    """Launch only useful K splits while preserving the matmul result."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(shrink_op, "is_batch_invariant", False)
    monkeypatch.setattr(lora_utils, "is_batch_invariant", False)
    monkeypatch.setattr(lora_utils, "load_lora_op_config", lambda *args: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        shrink_op, "get_lora_op_configs", lora_utils.get_lora_op_configs.__wrapped__
    )
    kernel, grids = shrink_op._lora_shrink_kernel, []

    class RecordShrink:
        def __getitem__(self, grid):
            grids.append(grid)
            return kernel[grid]

    monkeypatch.setattr(shrink_op, "_lora_shrink_kernel", RecordShrink())
    torch.set_default_device(device)
    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
    set_random_seed(0)
    check_lora_shrink_kernel(
        batches=batches,
        num_loras=4,
        rank=16,
        hidden_size=hidden_size,
        nslices=nslices,
        dtype=dtype,
        device=device,
        seq_length=1,
        scaling=0.5,
    )
    assert len(grids) == 1
    assert grids[0][:2] == (expected_grid_m, nslices)

"""Local A/B measurement; uses the real shrink entry point and metadata."""
import inspect
import json
import statistics
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops.lora_shrink_op as op
import vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops.utils as utils
from vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops import LoRAKernelMeta

assert torch.cuda.is_available()
assert not op.is_batch_invariant
assert utils.envs.VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER is None
source = inspect.getsource(op._lora_shrink)
new = 'SPLIT_K = min(kernel_config["split_k"], triton.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K))'
old = 'SPLIT_K = kernel_config["split_k"]'
assert source.count(new) == 1
namespace = dict(op.__dict__)
exec(compile(source.replace(new, old), "<baseline-shrink>", "exec"), namespace)
baseline = namespace["_lora_shrink"]
candidate = op._lora_shrink
results = []
for m, k, num_loras, nslices in [(32,4096,1,1), (32,4096,16,1),
                               (32,4096,32,1), (32,4096,16,3),
                               (32,256,4,1), (128,4096,16,1)]:
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    x = torch.randn((m,k), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    weights = [torch.randn((num_loras,16,k), device="cuda", dtype=x.dtype)
               for _ in range(nslices)]
    mapping = torch.arange(m,device="cuda",dtype=torch.int32) % num_loras
    mapping[-1] = -1
    meta = LoRAKernelMeta.make(num_loras,m,device="cuda")
    meta.prepare_tensors(mapping)
    args = meta.meta_args(token_nums=m,specialize_active_lora=False)
    outputs = [torch.empty((nslices,m,16),device="cuda",dtype=torch.float32)
               for _ in range(2)]
    utils._LORA_A_PTR_DICT.clear()
    for f,out in zip((baseline,candidate),outputs):
        for _ in range(5):
            f(x,weights,out,*args,0.5)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    ref = torch.zeros((nslices,m,16),dtype=torch.float64)
    for s,w in enumerate(weights):
        for lid in range(num_loras):
            mask = mapping.cpu() == lid
            ref[s,mask] = 0.5*x.cpu().double()[mask] @ w.cpu().double()[lid].T
    for out in outputs:
        torch.testing.assert_close(out.cpu().double(),ref,rtol=1e-2,atol=1e-2)
    graphs = []
    for f,out in zip((baseline,candidate),outputs):
        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
            for _ in range(200):
                f(x,weights,out,*args,0.5)
        graphs.append(graph)
    samples = [[],[]]
    for repeat in range(7):
        for which in ((0,1) if repeat % 2 == 0 else (1,0)):
            start,end = (torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(2))
            start.record()
            for _ in range(20):
                graphs[which].replay()
            end.record()
            end.synchronize()
            samples[which].append(start.elapsed_time(end)*1000/4000)
    medians = [statistics.median(times) for times in samples]
    row = dict(m=m,k=k,num_loras=num_loras,nslices=nslices,
               baseline_us=medians[0],candidate_us=medians[1],
               speedup=medians[0]/medians[1],samples_us=samples)
    results.append(row)
    print(json.dumps(row),flush=True)
    del graphs, outputs, weights, x, meta
    utils._LORA_A_PTR_DICT.clear()
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
report = dict(torch=torch.__version__,cuda=torch.version.cuda,
              gpu=torch.cuda.get_device_name(),results=results,
              method="7 alternating A/B rounds; 200 calls/graph x 20 replays; includes output zeroing; FP16, rank16, scaling0.5")
Path(__file__).with_name("gpu-benchmark.json").write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2))
```

import vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops.lora_shrink_op as op
import vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops.utils as utils

assert utils.envs.VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER is None

assert source.count(new) == 1
if args.arm == 'baseline':
    source = source.replace('def _lora_shrink(', 'def _baseline(').replace(new, old)
    exec(compile(source, '<baseline-shrink>', 'exec'), op.__dict__)
    op._lora_shrink.__wrapped__.__code__ = op._baseline.__wrapped__.__code__

llm = LLM(model=model_path, enable_lora=True, max_loras=args.loras,
          max_lora_rank=16, dtype='float16', max_model_len=128,
          max_num_seqs=4, max_num_batched_tokens=128, gpu_memory_utilization=0.4,
          kv_cache_memory_bytes=32*1024*1024, enforce_eager=True,
          attention_config={'backend': 'TRITON_ATTN'}, enable_prefix_caching=False,
          seed=0)
prompts = ['The capital of France is',
           'Write a short Python function that adds two numbers.',
           'Explain why the sky is blue in one sentence.',
           'The result of 2 + 2 is']
requests = [LoRARequest(f'adapter-{lid}', lid, str(root / f'adapter-{lid}'))
            for lid in ([1] * 4 if args.loras == 1 else [1, 2, 3, 4])]

class RecordKernel:
    def __getitem__(self, grid):
        def launch(*kernel_args, **kernel_kwargs):
            grids[tuple(grid)] += 1
            values = dict(zip(kernel.arg_names, kernel_args))
            values.update(kernel_kwargs)
            m, k, bk, split = (values[name] for name in ('M','K','BLOCK_K','SPLIT_K'))

            partitions[(m,k,bk,split)] += 1
            seen_lora_slots.update(lid for lid in values['lora_ids'].cpu().tolist() if lid >= 0)
            return kernel[grid](*kernel_args, **kernel_kwargs)

assert len(seen_lora_slots) == args.loras, seen_lora_slots
assert any(k//bk < split for (m,k,bk,split) in partitions) if args.arm == 'baseline' else any(split < 64 for (m,k,bk,split) in partitions)

                           logprobs=[float(p[t].logprob) for t,p in
                                     zip(completion.token_ids,completion.logprobs)]))
    samples.append(elapsed)
    records.append(record)

              pid=os.getpid(), model='Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B', revision=revision,
              adapter_hashes=json.loads((root / 'adapters.json').read_text()),
              config=dict(batch=4,rank=16,dtype='float16',eager=True,
                          output_tokens_per_request=16,kv_cache_bytes=32*1024*1024,
                          max_model_len=128,attention='TRITON_ATTN',prefix_cache=False),
              torch=torch.__version__,cuda=torch.version.cuda,gpu=torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
              recorded_grids=[dict(grid=list(g),calls=count) for g,count in grids.items()],
              actual_lora_slots=sorted(seen_lora_slots),
              partitions=[dict(m=m,k=k,block_k=bk,split_k=split,calls=count)
                          for (m,k,bk,split),count in partitions.items()],
              samples_seconds=samples,process_median_seconds=statistics.median(samples),
              output_tokens_per_second=[64/s for s in samples],outputs=records)

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Cap LoRA shrink's configured split-K at the number of K blocks to avoid launching empty reduction programs. Fixes #61030; the proposed cap and original H100 evidence are credited to @ToukoUrsin. The final diff changes one production line; the added boundary test and its dedicated imports have been removed following review.

## Claims

- With the default small-batch config and K=4096, reduce split-K from 64 to 16, removing 48 empty programs per M/N tile and adapter.
- Preserve useful K-block assignments and the fixed batch-invariant partition. Configs already at or below the cap retain their split count.
- Local kernel measurements show lower shrink latency in capped cases. The small-model E2E measurements below do not establish a reliable end-to-end speedup.

## Validation

Local hardware: NVIDIA RTX 3050 Laptop GPU (4GB), Ubuntu 24.04 / WSL2, driver 592.82, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1. The removed boundary test is retained only as an external validation script and is not part of the PR or CI.

```bash

.venv/bin/python -m pytest /path/to/test_review_boundaries.py -v
# 16 passed in 15.81s: FP16/BF16; K=255/256/257/4096/14337/16384/32768, M=32/128.
.venv/bin/python /path/to/verify_baseline.py
# 10 expected launch-grid failures, 6 passed in 5.61s on the uncapped baseline.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_lora_shrink_batch_invariant.py -v
# 6 passed in 2.99s, including bitwise equality across batch sizes.
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py
# All applicable hooks passed; normal commit hooks also passed.
git diff 3e8e136...HEAD --check
# Passed.
```

Both boundary arms execute the real Triton kernel and compare output with the existing matmul reference. The uncapped failures are expected reproducer results, not failing candidate tests. The existing batch-invariant suite remains unchanged. Full upstream GPU CI, H100, AMD, and XPU validation have not been run locally.

Kernel A/B: FP16, rank16, scaling0.5, default config, includes output zeroing; same tensors and mapping, including a no-LoRA token. Each CUDA graph contains 200 shrink calls. Seven alternating A/B and B/A rounds each replay the graph 20 times; values below are per-call median microseconds, with min/max across the seven rounds. Both paths also pass an FP64 matmul reference comparison at rtol/atol=1e-2.

| M / K / LoRA slots / slices | Baseline μs [min, max] | Capped μs [min, max] | Median ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 32 / 4096 / 1 / 1 | 7.63 [6.14, 8.24] | 5.46 [4.66, 7.31] | 1.40× |
| 32 / 4096 / 16 / 1 | 32.69 [31.25, 33.30] | 21.23 [20.45, 22.66] | 1.54× |
| 32 / 4096 / 32 / 1 | 60.32 [59.44, 64.53] | 36.57 [35.80, 41.00] | 1.65× |
| 32 / 4096 / 16 / 3 | 189.02 [187.36, 196.05] | 70.96 [69.92, 75.19] | 2.66× |
| 32 / 256 / 4 / 1 | 8.91 [8.21, 9.08] | 3.75 [3.45, 4.66] | 2.38× |
| 128 / 4096 / 16 / 1 (uncapped control) | 23.69 [23.25, 25.15] | 23.87 [23.65, 25.50] | 0.99× |

The kernel measurements were collected on the preceding base `bd5bbce`; both affected source files were identical after rebasing to `3e8e136`. This microbenchmark calls independently compiled baseline and candidate functions and is unaffected by the E2E correction below. The original issue's H100 measurements are separate author-provided evidence.

**Correction to previously reported E2E evidence:** the old harness replaced the outer `inference_mode` wrapper's code object without changing the function captured by its closure. Both arms therefore used the capped implementation. The previously reported 1.3382s/1.3408s comparison and 0.01084149 logprob difference are withdrawn as baseline/candidate evidence. The replacement harness changes the underlying `__wrapped__` function and verifies the actual kernel partition arguments before timing.

Corrected E2E: pinned Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, synthetic nonzero rank16/alpha16 LoRA on q/v/o/gate/up/down, FP16, eager TRITON_ATTN, no prefix caching, four requests × 16 greedy output tokens, max_model_len128, KV cache32MiB. One configuration uses the same adapter for all requests; the other uses four distinct adapters, one per request. Adapter tensor hashes match across every arm.

Each configuration runs three alternating AB/BA rounds, with a fresh process and engine for each arm: 12 processes total. Each engine performs one instrumented warmup followed by three complete generations without launch recording. Times exclude initialization and warmup; they include prefill, decoding, sampling, and host generation overhead, with CUDA synchronization around generation. The table reports the median of three process medians and the min/max of those process medians. The GPU is a laptop desktop device; clock and background-load variation were not controlled.

| Active LoRAs | Baseline seconds [range] | Capped seconds [range] | Baseline / capped | Output tokens/s baseline / capped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1.1106 [1.0901, 1.1679] | 1.2851 [1.1079, 1.2924] | 0.864× | 57.63 / 49.80 |
| 4 | 1.2531 [1.0609, 1.4145] | 1.1358 [1.1243, 1.1537] | 1.103× | 51.07 / 56.35 |

All generated token IDs matched across the 18 measured generations per configuration (1,152 output tokens/configuration, 2,304 total). Across the first measured generation of each paired baseline/candidate round, the maximum generated-token logprob difference was 0.00814527 for one active LoRA and 0.01142752 for four. This is observed equality on four synthetic-adapter prompts, not a general accuracy or bitwise-determinism guarantee.

Warmup recording verified one/four actual active LoRA slots and baseline SPLIT_K=64 versus capped SPLIT_K=4/8/12 at K=1024/2048/3072, BLOCK_K=256, during prefill and decode. Recording and GPU-to-CPU metadata reads were removed before timing. The one-adapter capped median is slower and the four-adapter capped median is faster, with overlapping run ranges; these mixed results do not support a reliable E2E speedup claim. This is an in-process integration smoke test, not an HTTP concurrency benchmark or trained-adapter task evaluation; larger deployment workloads remain unmeasured.

## Details

The default config for M<128 requests 64 splits with BLOCK_K=256. When the configured split count exceeds ceil(K/BLOCK_K), only the first ceil(K/BLOCK_K) splits have valid K data, each with one K iteration. The cap removes empty splits without changing useful tile assignments. `EVEN_K` is recomputed afterward, and the existing batch-invariant override still sets BLOCK_K=256 and SPLIT_K=8.

Ordinary multi-split accumulation still uses floating-point atomics and is not bitwise deterministic. Reducing to one split switches to direct stores, verified locally at K=255/256. The change adds no device synchronization and changes no operator schemas or default configuration tables.

Duplicate-work checks repeated before this review update found only this PR referencing #61030 and no other PR implementing this cap. #59572 optimizes the M-dimension grid; #50278 forces split-K=1 for determinism; #58533 changes PDL shrink/expand overlap and explicitly excludes the separate split-K optimization. This PR preserves split-K parallelism up to the useful K-block count.

**AI assistance:** OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and this description. The human submitter previously confirmed reviewing the original changed lines, understanding the validation limits, and personally running the relevant tests. This review update removes the contributed test and corrects/supplements the validation evidence; no new human execution of these supplementary measurements is claimed. All three commits include `Assisted-by` attribution and `Signed-off-by` trailers.

I've now run a fresh-process E2E integration comparison with Qwen3-0.6B, synthetic rank16 LoRAs, and four requests generating 16 greedy tokens each on an RTX 3050 Laptop GPU (4GB).
